Claim.description: A collection claim in force for one identifier: the client that is its collector, when the claim ends, and whether the claimant may still renew it. A claim released by a party other than its claimant, or whose claimant's access control entry no longer gives it standing in the context, is not renewable and still ends at `endsAt`, because the claimant is still connected until its own clock tells it to stop (VTI-NTF-084).

claimant.description: The client holding the claim: the subject of the access control entry it was granted to.

endsAt.description: When the claim ends unless renewed. The claimant stops collecting before this instant less its clock-skew tolerance; the VTA resumes no earlier than this instant plus its own (VTI-NTF-083, VTI-NTF-084).

renewable.description: Whether the claimant may renew the claim with vta/collection/claim before it ends.

Claim.title: Claim

CollectionEntry.description: The collection state of one identifier. `claim` is present exactly when `collector` is `client`, and `notCollectedReason` exactly when it is `none`.
CollectionEntry.title: CollectionEntry

Collector.description: Who collects for an identifier: `vta`, the VTA itself; `client`, the claimant of a collection claim in force; or `none`, nobody, for the reason given in `notCollectedReason`.
Collector.title: Collector

ContextId.description: The trust context the identifier belongs to.
ContextId.title: ContextId

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

NotCollectedReason.description: Why nobody collects for an identifier the VTA would otherwise collect for: `limit`, the VTA is at the bound it states on the number of identifiers it collects for (VTI-NTF-088); `conflict`, another connection for the identifier kept closing the VTA's, and the VTA stopped after the bound it states until the conflict is resolved (VTI-NTF-085). `disabled`, collection by default is disabled for the identifier's trust context — by the context's own setting, or because the VTA's operator has suspended it for every context — so the VTA collects for no identifier there that a client has not claimed (VTI-NTF-097, VTI-NTF-098); vta/collection/settings/show says which.
NotCollectedReason.title: NotCollectedReason

Response.description: One page of the identifiers that match.

nextCursor.description: Present when more items remain; absent on the last page.

schema.description: A client with standing in a trust context lists, for every identifier there that its VTA collects for unless a client has claimed it, who collects for it now: the VTA, a claimant — with the claim's end and whether it can be renewed — or nobody, and why (VTI-NTF-091). The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

collector.description: Only identifiers with this collector — `none`, for instance, to find the identifiers nobody collects for.

cursor.description: An opaque cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor`, for the same filters. The VTA refuses one it did not issue.
